Roasted Chestnuts

Served at: Martinstag Lantern Evening

Serves 4-6Prep 15 minCook 20-30 min

Roasted Chestnuts are a quintessential autumn treat, especially cherished during Martinstag (St. Martin's Day) celebrations on November 11th. As families gather for lantern parades in the chilly evening air, the warm, earthy aroma and comforting taste of freshly roasted chestnuts provide a perfect, traditional snack to enjoy outdoors.

Ingredients

  • 1 pound (450 g) fresh chestnuts
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
  2. Using a sharp, serrated knife, carefully score an 'X' or a single slit across the flat, rounded side of each chestnut shell. This is crucial to prevent them from exploding during roasting.
  3. Optional: Place the scored chestnuts in a bowl of hot water and let them soak for 10-15 minutes. This helps them steam and makes peeling easier. Drain them thoroughly before roasting.
  4. Spread the chestnuts in a single layer on a sturdy baking sheet.
  5. Roast for 20-30 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until the shells begin to peel back and the insides are tender and slightly golden.
  6. Remove from the oven and immediately wrap the hot chestnuts in a clean kitchen towel for 5-10 minutes. The residual steam will further loosen the shells and inner skin.
  7. While still warm (but cool enough to handle), peel away the outer shell and the inner papery skin. Discard any chestnuts that appear moldy or dried out.
  8. Serve immediately, optionally sprinkled with a little salt, to warm up during your Martinstag festivities.

Tips

  • Always choose firm, heavy chestnuts without any holes or soft spots, which can indicate worms or spoilage.
  • Peel chestnuts while they are still warm; they become much harder to peel once they cool completely.
  • For an authentic experience, if you have a fireplace, you can roast them in a special long-handled chestnut pan or a cast-iron skillet with holes over hot coals.
